audit.whatIsWrong: Four separate content strings say Purge gives Urgot move speed to close the gap: wants.foe[0] 'Walk you down with W's move speed', wants.you[1] 'never let his W move-speed close the gap', whys[3] 'W's move speed lets him walk through your range', and mid 'he can walk through your chip with W's move speed'. Purge does the opposite — it slows him.
audit.why: Riot's own text is 'Urgot slows himself while he unloads his weapon on nearby enemies', and the derived flag on W is slow. This is not a naming quibble, it inverts the entire lane plan. The entry teaches Mel that an Urgot pressing W is closing on her and that she must retreat; in fact an Urgot channelling Purge is the slowest he ever gets and that is her free poke window. A 20% win rate is exactly what you would expect from a player backing off during the one window she should be attacking. Urgot's actual gap-closer is Disdain (E), a 475-range charge on 16s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Purge slows Urgot while he channels it. His gap-close is Disdain (E), 16s at rank 1 — that is the cooldown to track, and Purge is the window to poke.
sources: champ-data/_kits/urgot.json (W Purge: 'Urgot slows himself while he unloads his weapon on nearby enemies'; flags: slow)

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early states flatly: 'your W barrier eats projectiles but his legs are point-blank shotguns, not projectiles, so it does nothing here'. Meanwhile the full layer's dosFull[1].t says 'Hold W Rebuttal for Disdain (Flip)'. The two layers give opposite instructions about Mel's defining ability.
audit.why: Three of Urgot's five abilities carry the projectile flag: Corrosive Charge (Q), Disdain (E) and Fear Beyond Death (R). The half of the sentence about his legs is right — Echoing Flames (P) and Purge (W) are point-blank and not projectiles — but the conclusion drawn from it is false. Rebuttal has real targets here, and the most important one is Fear Beyond Death, the projectile execute that the same content layer calls the thing that ends you. Telling a Mel player her W 'does nothing' against Urgot removes her only answer to his ultimate.
audit.corrected: His legs are not projectiles, but Corrosive Charge and Fear Beyond Death are — hold Rebuttal for the chem-drill, not for chip.
sources: champ-data/_kits/urgot.json (Q flags: projectile, dash, slow; E flags: projectile, hardCC, shield; R Fear Beyond Death flags: projectile, hardCC, slow, execute)

audit.whatIsWrong: The 'shotgun legs' are attributed to Q and W throughout — 'his shotgun legs (Q/W)', 'His Q/W shotgun legs come online', 'shotgun-leg you with percent-max-HP Q/W'. The legs are Echoing Flames (P).
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Urgot's basic attacks and Purge periodically trigger blasts of flame from his legs.' So the legs fire off his autos and off Purge — never off Q. Corrosive Charge is a lobbed explosive at a target location on 10s at rank 1, a completely different threat that Mel can sidestep and that Rebuttal can catch. Merging them into one 'Q/W' blob means the player cannot tell the dodgeable ranged spell from the unavoidable close-range chip, which is the whole spacing decision in this lane.
audit.corrected: Echoing Flames (P) fires off his autos and Purge at close range. Corrosive Charge (Q) is a separate ranged explosive on 10s at rank 1.
sources: champ-data/_kits/urgot.json (P Echoing Flames: 'basic attacks and Purge periodically trigger blasts of flame from his legs'; Q Corrosive Charge cd 10/9.5/9/8.5/8, range 800)

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet logs 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere' and it is accurate — neither layer contains a single cooldown number for either champion, despite both layers being built around 'wait for Disdain to be down'.
audit.why: The numbers make the advice usable and one of them settles the lane's central question. Solar Snare is 11s at rank 1; Disdain is 16s at rank 1. Mel's root comes back five seconds faster than his charge, which means holding E purely as an anti-engage tool is affordable — she is not giving up poke tempo to do it. Without those two numbers the instruction 'save your root for his flip' reads as a pure sacrifice and players will not follow it. Purge is also worth stating: 12/9/6/3/0, so by rank 5 it is permanently available and the close-range chip never stops.
audit.corrected: Solar Snare 11s at rank 1 vs Disdain 16s at rank 1 — your root outpaces his charge, so holding it costs you nothing. Purge reaches 0s cooldown at rank 5.
sources: champ-data/_kits/urgot.json (E cd 16/15.5/15/14.5/14; W cd 12/9/6/3/0; R cd 100/85/70)

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet logs that the entry never names an Urgot ability. The ultimate is called 'His Fear (R)' and 'R Fear-and-execute'; the real name is Fear Beyond Death.
audit.why: Named abilities are what a player can match against the enemy bar mid-game. 'Fear' is also actively misleading — it suggests a fear/flee crowd-control effect, when Fear Beyond Death is a chem-drill projectile that impales and then executes below a health threshold.
audit.corrected: Fear Beyond Death (R), 100s at rank 1, projectile, impales then executes under the threshold.
sources: champ-data/_kits/urgot.json (R Fear Beyond Death, cd 100/85/70, flags projectile/hardCC/slow/execute)

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer rates this EVEN at 5.5/10 with all seven phases marked 'Skill', and its tldr reads 'He can't reach you and you reflect what he throws' with a win condition of 'Stack, snare, and execute — he never gets to play'. The recorded win rate is 20% and content.win gives Urgot levels 4 through 2+ items.
audit.why: This is the widest gap between the two layers anywhere in my slice. The content layer says 'This is where you lose the lane', 'Hug your turret... and pray for ganks', and 'You don't out-scale him in this specific lane'. The full layer says he never gets to play. Both render on the same page. The sample is only 5 games so I am not treating 20% as precise, but the direction is corroborated by the content layer's own narrative and by the kit: Urgot has a charge, a shield on it, and an execute, against a mage with no dash.
audit.corrected: HARD at 7.5/10, with the headline rewritten to match the body text.
sources: champ-data/content/mel.js (win[] gives Urgot levels 4-5, 6, First item, 2+ items)

notes: This was the weakest entry in my slice and I gave it the most work — the packet flagged all three defect types at once (no sequencing anywhere, no ability names, a suspect name) and the underlying problem was worse than any of those: the content layer had Urgot's W backwards. THE BIG ONE: four content strings say Purge gives Urgot move speed to walk Mel down. Riot's text is 'Urgot slows himself while he unloads his weapon on nearby enemies'. The entry was telling players to retreat during the single window Urgot is slowest, which plausibly contributes to the 20% recorded win rate. Everything downstream of that — wants.foe[0], wants.you[1], whys[3], mid — had to move together, so those four edits are one correction, not four. SECOND: content.early asserted Rebuttal 'does nothing here' because his legs are not projectiles. His legs are not, but Corrosive Charge (Q), Disdain (E) and Fear Beyond Death (R) all carry the projectile flag. The full layer meanwhile said 'Hold W Rebuttal for Disdain (Flip)'. The two layers were giving opposite instructions on Mel's signature ability, and the content layer's version removes her only answer to his execute. UNVERIFIED, NOT ASSERTED EITHER WAY: (a) the content layer calls his damage 'percent-max-HP' in four places. Urgot's kit carries no percentHealth flag anywhere, while the same library does derive that flag for other champions (Swain's passive), so the claim is unsupported here — but flag absence is not proof and I did not want to strip a damage-profile claim on that basis. I removed the phrase only where I was already rewriting the string for the W error, and left it standing elsewhere. Worth a wiki check on Purge's damage. (b) The original text said Solar Snare can 'cancel his E flip'. Whether a root interrupts Disdain mid-charge is a dash-interaction question the kit files cannot answer, so I rephrased to 'root him as he steps to charge' — preventing the charge rather than cancelling it — which is true regardless of how the interrupt resolves. I moved this from EVEN 5.5/10 to HARD 7.5/10 on a 5-game sample, which is thin. I did it because the content layer independently describes a losing lane in three separate strings and because the full layer's 'he never gets to play' is indefensible against a champion with a shielded charge and an execute. If you disagree with the exact number, the direction is still the point.
